report:
**Conclusion:** Medical evidence does not support the claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) buildup (hypercapnia).

**Key Findings:**

1. **Gas Permeability:** $\text{CO}_2$ and oxygen molecules are infinitely smaller than the microscopic weave of cloth or surgical masks. Carbon dioxide passes freely through the material and escapes around the loose edges of the mask during exhalation.
2. **Physiological Safety:** Clinical evaluations reviewed in a [CDC Science Brief](https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/science/science-briefs/masking-science-sars-cov2.html) demonstrate that wearing cloth or surgical masks produces no clinically meaningful changes in blood oxygen or $\text{CO}_2$ levels, even among older adults and individuals with chronic lung diseases such as COPD.
3. **Discomfort vs. Toxicity:** People sometimes confuse sensory discomfort—such as warmth, trapped humidity, or breathing resistance—with hypercapnia or oxygen deprivation. Fact-check evaluations by [USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/) and [Science Feedback](https://science.feedback.org/review/facebook-posts-spread-unsupported-anonymous-claim-that-face-mask-use-caused-a-lung-infection-in-a-healthy-teenager/) confirm that this local microclimate effect does not alter internal blood gas levels or cause toxicity.

In summary, standard cloth and surgical face masks allow normal gas exchange and do not trap dangerous levels of carbon dioxide.

**Sources:**
* [CDC Science Brief: Community Use of Masks](https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/science/science-briefs/masking-science-sars-cov2.html)
* [USA Today Fact Check: Wearing Face Mask Will Not Cause Hypoxia or Hypercapnia](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/)
* [Science Feedback Review on Face Masks and Hypercapnia](https://science.feedback.org/review/facebook-posts-spread-unsupported-anonymous-claim-that-face-mask-use-caused-a-lung-infection-in-a-healthy-teenager/)
